3754.t: From Proto-Indo-European *swe-dʰh₁- (“custom, character”), from the reflexive pronoun *swé (“self”) + *dʰeh₁- (“to put, place, set”), equivalent to the acc. ἕ (hé) of οὗ (hoû, “him”) + τίθημι (títhēmi, “to set”).

3796.t: Related to βῆναι (bênai), aorist of βαίνω (baínō, “step”), though the exact morphology is uncertain.

3784.t: Borrowed from Proto-Scythian *Skuδi. Cognate with Akkadian 𒆳𒅖𒆪𒍝𒀀𒀀 (Iškuzāya), 𒇽𒅖𒆪𒍝𒀀𒀀 (Iškuzāya).

3792.t: Inherited from Proto-Hellenic *gʷorā́, itself from Proto-Indo-European *gʷorh₃éh₂, whence also Latin vorō.

3794.t: From Proto-Indo-European *gʷrebʰ-. Cognates include Old Church Slavonic жрѣбѧ (žrěbę) ("foal") and Irish bromach ("colt").

3749.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₁rewg- (“to belch, roar”). Cognates include Latin ērūgō, Old Armenian ործամ (orcam), Lithuanian riaugėti, Russian рыга́ть (rygátʹ), Old English rocettan and Albanian regj.

3720.t: Disputed. Perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *h₂leg- (“to care”), and related to ἀλέγω (alégō, “to take care”).

3779.t: From Proto-Hellenic *wródon, borrowed from some Eastern language, most likely Proto-Iranian *wardah (“flower, rose”) (compare Mycenaean Greek 𐀺𐀈𐀸 (wo-do-we), Old Persian *vr̥dah, Aramaic 𐡅𐡀𐡓𐡃𐡀 (warda), Classical Syriac ܘܪܕܐ (wardā), Old Armenian վարդ…

3713.t: From ἄστε(ϝ) (áste(w)), the oblique stem of ἄστυ (ástu, “town”), + -ιος (-ios, adjective suffix). For the opposition with ἄγροικος (ágroikos), compare typologically Latin cīvīlis, urbānus vs. agrestis, pāgānus, rūsticus.

3795.t: Connected with βάσκειν (báskein, “to slander”), which is probably from βάζω (bázō, “to speak, say”), but might be related to Latin fascinum (“witchcraft; penis”), in which case both would derive from a European substrate language.

3765.t: From ὁμοιόω (homoióō, “to make like, to be like”) + -σις (-sĭs).

3719.t: Traditionally derived from Proto-Indo-European *h₂éngos, from the root *h₂eng- (“to curve”), though Beekes prefers deriving the word from a Pre-Greek stratum, due to its semantic domain; many words for "vessel" are mentioned by Homer but are loaned from…

3710.t: According to the LIV, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂r̥-né-s-ti, from *h₂res- (“to refuse, deny”).

3751.t: From ἑξήκοντα (hexḗkonta, “sixty”) + -στός (-stós), a variant of -τός (-tós, ordinal suffix).

3778.t: The suffixes -ινος (-īnos) and -ινη (-īnē) are found both with inherited and with Pre-Greek substrate words. Since there are no good cognates, however, the word is probably Pre-Greek.

3777.t: From ῥάπτω (rhắptō, “to sew together, stitch”) + -η (-ē, action noun suffix).

3776.t: From ὑφάζω (hŭphắzō, “to weave”, from ὑφαίνω (hŭphaínō, “to weave”) + -άζω (-ắzō, verbal suffix)) + -μα (-mă, nominal suffix).

3762.t: From the radical *ὀπ- (from Proto-Indo-European *h₃ekʷ-), the same root of ὄμμα (ómma, “eye”).

3767.t: It could derive from Proto-Indo-European *h₃nebʰ- (“navel”), but the semantic explanation as a navel-like knob is hardly convincing. Furnée connects ἀμφίας (amphías, “bad Sicilian wine”) and ἀμφής (amphḗs, “wine blossom”).

3797.t: According to Beekes, the word is probably Pre-Greek, in view of the numerous variations and the suffix -ιτον (-iton).

3728.t: From ἐκ- (ek-, “out, away, off”) + ζέω (zéō, “to boil; to ferment”).

3774.t: From ὑστερέω (husteréō, “to come late, to lag behind; to fail to obtain, to lack”) + -μα (-mă, nominal suffix), from ὕστερος (hústeros, “latter, later”) + -έω (-éō, verbal suffix).
